conditions.overall: Wild water is fishing well in smaller, cooler, higher-elevation creeks, with larger wild streams experiencing pressure and occasional warm temperatures. Delayed harvest streams are approximately two weeks away from stocking beginning.

tactics: Focus on small wild creeks that are off the beaten path — these are holding the happiest fish with the most production right now.
Avoid larger wild streams on warmer days as they are on the cusp of being too warm and have seen heavy pressure all summer.
Fish smaller, cooler streams at higher elevation for the best wild trout action.
Light and small dry dropper rigs have been the name of the game in wild water.
For delayed harvest streams, use the NC daily stocking report tool to confirm a stream has been stocked before making the trip, as stocking dates are spread out across October and November.
Check the NC daily stocking report consistently, as it is updated daily and stocking windows vary by stream this season.

elevation_note: High Country streams (Boone, 3300-4000ft) run 1-2 weeks behind lower-elevation WNC
stocking_note: Delayed harvest stocking begins around two weeks out (from September 18, 2026). This year stockings are more spread out throughout October and November rather than concentrated at the start of the month. Scheduled windows: Helton Creek Sept 28–Oct 2; Big Horse Creek Oct 5–9; Watauga River (Valle Crucis & Lower DH), New River (Todd Island Park), and Wilson Creek Oct 12–16. Use the NC daily stocking report tool to confirm before fishing.
